hero.title: Manage your tasks with <g>clarity</g> and ease.
hero.subtitle: See the same tasks as a list, a board, a calendar or a timeline. Invite your team and decide who can see and change what.
hero.note: No payment details needed. Works in any modern browser and installs like an app.

features.title: Everything you need to stay organized
features.subtitle: A focused toolset for planning, tracking and sharing work, without the clutter.

views.title: Four views of the same tasks
views.desc: Switch between a list with inline editing, a kanban board, a month calendar and a timeline. Edit in any of them and the others stay in sync.

dependencies.title: Dependencies and conflicts
dependencies.desc: Mark tasks that must finish first. The timeline draws the links and flags a task that starts before its prerequisite is due.

roles.title: Roles and permissions
roles.desc: Invite people by email with a role. Five built-in roles, plus custom roles with exactly the permissions you choose.

comments.title: Comments and attachments
comments.desc: Discuss a task where the work lives and attach files to it, so context does not get lost in chat.

install.title: Installable on any device
install.desc: Add TaskMan to your home screen or desktop. Layouts adapt to phones, and the app tells you when you are offline.

secure.title: Secure by default
secure.desc: Verified email addresses, password reset by email, and a password change that signs out your other devices.

teams.title: Everyone sees what they need, and nothing more.
teams.description: Every workspace comes with five roles. Pages and actions a role does not allow are hidden, and the server enforces the same rules.

invite.title: Invite by email
invite.desc: Pick a role when you send the invitation. People accept it from the link in their inbox.

custom.title: Create custom roles
custom.desc: Combine permissions for tasks, projects, reports, members and settings into a role that fits your team.

access.title: Change access any time
access.desc: Update a role or remove a member from the team page. Regenerate the invite code if it leaks.

cta.title: Ready to organize your work?
cta.titleBack: Ready to get back to work?
cta.description: Create an account, name your workspace and add your first task in a couple of minutes.
cta.descriptionBack: Jump back into your workspace and pick up where you left off.

help.contact: Ask a workspace owner first, as they can manage members and invite codes from the Team page. For product questions or bug reports, email <m>support@taskman.io</m> with the page you were on and what you expected to happen.

what-is-workspace.a: A workspace holds your projects, tasks and team. Everything you see is scoped to the workspace you are in. Use the workspace switcher at the top of the sidebar to move between workspaces.

create-first-task.q: How do I create my first task?
create-first-task.a: Open Tasks in the sidebar and choose Add Task. Give it a title, a due date and a priority. A start date, assignee, labels and prerequisites are optional.

invite-teammates.a: Open Team and invite people by email, choosing a role for each invitation. You can also share the invite code from the dashboard or Settings. Anyone who joins with the invite code starts as a Viewer.

regenerate-invite.q: What happens when I regenerate the invite code?
regenerate-invite.a: The old code and links stop working straight away. People who already joined keep their access.

four-views.q: What are the four task views?
four-views.a: List, Board, Calendar and Timeline. They show the same tasks and stay in sync. Switch between them with the view switcher on the Tasks page.

share-filters.q: Can I share a filtered view with a teammate?
share-filters.a: Yes. The search, filters and sort you choose on the Tasks page are kept in the address, so copy the link and send it. Whoever opens it sees the same layout and filters, within the tasks their role can see.

saved-views.q: How do I save a view?
saved-views.a: Set the layout and filters you want, open Views on the Tasks page and choose Save current view. Give it a name, and tick Share with the workspace if teammates should see it too. Open Manage views to rename or delete the views you saved. Workspace admins can also rename or delete shared views.

my-work.q: Where do I see only my tasks?
my-work.a: The dashboard starts with My work: your open tasks grouped as overdue, due today, this week and later. View all opens the Tasks page filtered to tasks assigned to you.

move-board.q: How do I change a task status on the Board?
move-board.a: Drag a card to another column (Pending, In Progress or Completed). Without a mouse, open the card menu and choose Move to.

inline-edit.q: Can I edit a task without opening it?
inline-edit.a: Yes. In the List view click a title, status, priority or date to edit it inline. The row actions menu is always reachable by keyboard.

dependencies.a: Pick prerequisites in the task form. The count shows on list rows and board cards, and the Timeline draws arrows between linked bars. Circular dependencies are rejected with the message "This dependency would create a cycle". Deleting a task removes it from the prerequisites of other tasks.

scheduling-conflict.a: A conflict appears when a task starts before its prerequisite is due. The Timeline shows a red dashed arrow so you can move one of the two dates.

subtasks.a: Yes. Open a task and add subtasks to break the work into smaller steps. Subtasks belong to their parent task.

scrum-structure.q: How are projects, sprints and tasks organised?
scrum-structure.a: Projects contain sprints, and sprints contain tasks. Tasks can have subtasks. The backlog holds the tasks of a project that are not in any sprint yet.

backlog.a: The backlog is every task in a project without a sprint. Plan work by moving backlog tasks into a sprint.

story-points.a: Story points are a relative estimate of effort for a task. Sprints add them up so you can compare planned work with what the team completes.

start-complete-sprint.q: How do I start and complete a sprint?
start-complete-sprint.a: Open the sprint in your project and choose Start sprint when planning is done. When the work is finished choose Complete sprint. You need permission to edit projects to do this.

burndown.a: The burndown chart shows the remaining story points of a sprint over time, so you can see whether the team is on track to finish.

system-roles.a:
Product Owner: full control of projects, tasks, team and settings.
Scrum Master: edits projects and tasks, and sees the team and reports.
Developer: edits tasks, and sees projects, the team and reports.
Team Member: edits tasks, and sees projects and reports.
Viewer: read-only access to projects, tasks and reports.

custom-roles.q: Can I create a custom role?
custom-roles.a: Yes. Go to Settings, then Roles and permissions, and choose New role. Tick exactly the permissions you want. System roles cannot be edited or deleted.

change-role.q: How do I change a member role or remove someone?
change-role.a: Owners and anyone allowed to manage users can use the role menu on a member row to change the role, and the bin button to remove the member.

hidden-pages.q: Why can I not see a page or button?
hidden-pages.a: Pages and buttons your role cannot use are hidden. Opening one by link shows an access message instead. Ask a workspace owner to change your role if you need access.

notifications-what.a: You are notified when someone assigns you a task, completes a task you own or are assigned to, mentions you in a comment, or comments on a task you own or are assigned to. They appear under the bell in the top bar and in your inbox, and are kept for 90 days. You never get a notification for your own actions.

notifications-mention.q: How do I mention someone in a comment?
notifications-mention.a: Type @ in a comment and pick a teammate from the list with the arrow keys and Enter, or tap a name. You can also type @FirstName or @First Last. Mentioned people are notified right away.

notifications-email.q: How do I choose which emails I get?
notifications-email.a: In-app notifications are always on. Under Settings, then Notifications, turn emails on or off: the general switch controls all emails, Task Assigned also covers mentions and comments on your tasks, and Task Completed covers finished tasks.

notifications-push.q: How do I get push notifications on my phone or computer?
notifications-push.a: Under Settings, then Notifications, open the Push section and choose Turn on for this device. Your browser asks for permission only then. Each device and browser is set up on its own, and the Send me push notifications switch (saved with Save preferences) pauses push on all of them. If you blocked notifications, allow them for this site in your browser settings and reload. On iPhone and iPad, add TaskMan to the Home Screen first and turn push on from the installed app. Push needs the server to be set up for it; if the Push section says it is not set up, ask your administrator.

edit-profile.q: Where do I edit my profile?
edit-profile.a: Under Settings, then Profile. You can change your name, job title and other details.

change-password.q: What happens when I change my password?
change-password.a: You are signed out of all your other devices. This device stays signed in, and the others must sign in again with the new password.

forgot-password.q: I forgot my password. What now?
forgot-password.a: Choose Forgot password on the sign-in page and we will email you a reset link.

session-expired.a: You stay signed in for 7 days on each device. After that, or if you sign a device out from Security > Signed-in devices, you return to the sign-in page. Your work is saved on the server.

install-pwa.q: Can I install TaskMan on my phone or computer?
install-pwa.a: Yes. TaskMan is a progressive web app. Use Add to Home Screen in your phone browser, or the install icon in the address bar on desktop.

bottom-nav.q: How do I navigate on a phone?
bottom-nav.a: On small screens the main pages are in a bottom navigation bar so they are reachable with one thumb. The full menu stays in the sidebar.

offline.a: Partly. The app shell and pages you already opened load without a connection, but offline mode is read-only. Reconnect to create or change anything.

shortcuts-list.a: Press ? anywhere in a workspace to see them all. The main ones: C creates a task, / searches tasks, and G followed by D, T, P, B, C or R jumps to the dashboard, tasks, projects, board, calendar or reports. Shortcuts pause while you type in a field or when a dialog is open, and they skip pages your role cannot open.

global-search.a: Press Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) to open search from anywhere. Press / on the Tasks page to jump to the task search box, or / on any other page to open search.

go-to-page.q: How do I jump to another page with the keyboard?
go-to-page.a: Press G, then within a second press D for the dashboard, T for tasks, P for projects, B for the board, C for the calendar or R for reports. If nothing happens, your role may not include that page.

gantt-keys.q: How do I move a bar on the Timeline with the keyboard?
gantt-keys.a: Focus a bar and press the left or right arrow to move it one day. Hold Shift with the arrows to resize the bar instead.

send-comment.q: How do I send a comment from the keyboard?
send-comment.a: Press Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on Mac) in the comment box.

calendar-today.q: Is there a shortcut to jump to today in the calendar?
calendar-today.a: Yes. Press T in the Calendar view to jump back to today.

data-access.q: Who can see my workspace data?
data-access.a: Only members of the workspace, limited by their role. Every request is checked against your role and the workspace on the server.

other-devices.q: How do I sign out other devices?
other-devices.a: Change your password. Doing so signs you out of every other device while keeping this one signed in.

report-problem.q: How do I report a bug or a security concern?
report-problem.a: Ask a workspace owner first. For product questions, bug reports or security concerns, email support@taskman.io with the page you were on and what you expected to happen.
